findings.description: The sync wrapper assigns `copy._local.statistics = self._local.statistics`, so the copy keeps its own stats dict rather than the shared `stats` dict. The async path assigns `stats` to both. As a result `wrapped_f.statistics` is cleared on each call but never updated during retries.
findings.rationale: Trigger: call any function decorated with sync @retry. `stats.clear()` empties the dict that `wrapped_f.statistics` points to. `copy._local.statistics` is set to `self._local.statistics`, which is the previous dict and not `stats`. The retry loop writes attempt_number and other values to that dict, so `wrapped_f.statistics` stays empty. This defeats the purpose of the change, and `fn.statistics` shows `{}` after the call. The same line also hands every call the same prior dict, which breaks isolation between nested or recursive calls.
